note: `at` is the second in the captured run where the beat starts speaking, so each line lands on what is actually on screen. The build fails if a beat runs past the next beat's start. Measured rate for this voice is about 0.09 s per character, which is what the anchors are spaced against; a rewrite that gets longer trips the check rather than quietly talking over the next line.

beats.text: This is Mitos. A fleet of institutional agents that finishes a chore, and can prove afterwards why it did each thing.
Five agents, catalogued by department. The router reads this catalogue to decide who wakes.
A pull request lands. Nobody opened Mitos. A webhook did this.
Every signal cites the exact hunk that raised it.
Three of three wake, because this change carries personal data.
The thread remembers. This service was here in July, and that deferral has now expired.
The gate rejects the first draft. The pull request carried a live looking credential, and an instruction telling the review agent to approve itself.
One write is proposed, addressed by its own sha256.
The reader identity cannot perform it. That is Google IAM refusing, outside this process.
Second run. No personal data this time, so compliance is skipped. The fleet is deciding, not following a pipeline.
And it recalls what the first run wrote, live, out of Firestore.
Every outcome walks back to the diff that caused it. That is the thread.

Three Cloud Run services under three separate service accounts, and every gate decision runs inside the agent framework's tool interceptor rather than in a prompt. Take Google Cloud away and that boundary becomes an if statement the agent is free to skip.
